page: Google Cloud Platform c3-standard-4-lssd is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the c3 server family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8481C processor running at 2.7 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes an L3 cache of 105 MB, alongside support for advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It also includes 402 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, while offering zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals average single-core CPU performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1714.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1617.89. However, multi-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by a Geekbench multi-core score of 3812.0 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression speed categorized in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with uncached read and write speeds of 29.2 GB/sec and 22.26 GB/sec respectively. Despite these constraints, the instance achieves average results in static web serving throughput at 6.5 GB/sec and single-threaded gzip compression at 26.36 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c3-standard-4-lssd balances dedicated compute resources and high-speed local NVMe storage within a modern hardware class. The inclusion of AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets provides specialized acceleration for cryptographic and vector operations without requiring discrete GPU hardware. This server is best suited for general-purpose workloads, static web serving, lightweight local-storage-dependent applications, and development environments that can leverage its dedicated CPU allocation and local SSD capacity.
